# Orchestrator background-dispatch hygiene: Monitor + bw-poll bridge + tool-loading + TaskOutput-forbidden-on-Agents

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-12 ariadne PLINY incident (same anchor as Ticket A). PLINY dispatched CAPTAIN_ADA via `Agent({ run_in_background: true, ... })` for synthetic corpus authoring. PRINCIPAL asked "is ADA stuck?" PLINY had no codified discipline for:

1. Capturing the returned `task_id` at dispatch time
2. Loading the deferred tools (`TaskStop`, `Monitor`) via `ToolSearch` at session start
3. Setting up a push-notification mechanism for CAPTAIN heartbeats
4. Knowing that `TaskOutput` is deprecated and reading an Agent's `.output` file overflows context

The discipline gap compounded with the tooling gap. PLINY confabulated rather than say "uncertain, checking." Filed separately as Ticket C (confabulation) and Ticket A (universal CAPTAIN heartbeat discipline). This ticket addresses the orchestrator-side dispatch hygiene specifically.

## Anthropic-side facts (as of 2026-05-12)

These shape what's actually possible vs aspirational; the discipline must reflect them honestly:

- **`Monitor` tool** ([release v2.1.98 on 2026-04-09](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w15)) — runs a shell command whose stdout streams as in-chat notifications. Persistent mode available for session-length watches. This is the canonical push channel for orchestrators.

- **`TaskStop` tool** — stops a running background task by `task_id`. Orchestrator can call it; CAPTAINs cannot ([issue #23154](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/23154)).

- **`TaskOutput` tool** — DEPRECATED per its own tool description. For Bash tasks, prefer reading the output file via the `Read` tool. **For Agent tasks, do NOT read the `.output` file** — it is a symlink to the full sub-agent conversation transcript (JSONL) and will overflow the orchestrator's context.

- **`PushNotification` tool** — orthogonal; pushes user-actionable events to PRINCIPAL's phone/desktop. Not the orchestrator-to-CAPTAIN or CAPTAIN-to-orchestrator channel.

- **No tool exists to enumerate running background tasks** ([issue #29011](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/29011), [issue #49140](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/49140)). The orchestrator MUST materialize task IDs to a checkable place (bw comment) at dispatch time, otherwise the information is structurally unrecoverable.

- **Subagents cannot run `TaskStop`** ([issue #23154](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/23154)). Background work spawned inside a CAPTAIN cannot be cleaned up by that CAPTAIN. Background-Bash and `Monitor` are forbidden in CAPTAINs (per Ticket A A5).

## The discipline

Canonical orchestrator dispatch sequence for any `run_in_background: true` Agent or Bash call:

### Step 1 — At orchestrator-session start: load deferred tools

`ToolSearch` with `select:TaskStop,Monitor,PushNotification` at session start (or first time the orchestrator needs them). This loads their schemas into the orchestrator's context so subsequent invocations work without per-call schema fetches.

`TaskOutput` is **not loaded** by default — it's deprecated. If a specific use case requires it (rare; only legacy bash polling), load it on demand with explicit awareness of the "do NOT read Agent .output files" caveat.

### Step 2 — At dispatch time: fire Agent + capture task_id + materialize to bw + start Monitor

```
# 1. Fire the Agent in background
task_result = Agent({ run_in_background: true, ... })
# captures task_id from the returned <task-notification>

# 2. Materialize task_id to bw immediately
bw comment <dispatch-ticket> "Dispatched <CAPTAIN> at <timestamp>. task_id=<id>. Brief: <link or summary>."

# 3. Start the persistent Monitor that polls bw for new comments
Monitor({
  command: <canonical bw-poll loop, see below>,
  description: "watching <CAPTAIN> heartbeats on <dispatch-ticket>",
  persistent: true
})
```

### Step 3 — Canonical bw-poll loop (template lives in the role file)

```bash
last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
while true; do
  bw show <dispatch-ticket> --json 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg since "$last" \
        '.comments[] | select(.timestamp > $since) | "[\(.author) \(.timestamp)] \(.body[:300])"' \
    || true
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  sleep 30
done
```

Each new bw comment by the CAPTAIN (or anyone else writing to the dispatch ticket) becomes a stdout line, which Monitor emits as an in-chat notification. The orchestrator reads `bw show` for full content when the notification fires.

### Step 4 — On CAPTAIN completion: TaskStop the Monitor + read verdict

```
# Wait for the Agent's completion notification (automatic; no polling needed)
# When the notification fires:
TaskStop(Monitor's task_id)  # tear down the watcher
# Read the Agent's tool result for the verdict (NOT the .output file)
# Comment the verdict outcome on the parent epic
```

### Step 5 — For genuinely actionable events: PushNotification to PRINCIPAL

For events PRINCIPAL needs to act on out-of-band (ship/no-ship verdict ready, blocker requiring human judgment, escalation), fire `PushNotification`. This is orthogonal to the orchestrator-in-chat Monitor notifications.

## Phase-A architectural decisions (LOCKED)

### B1. `TaskOutput` is forbidden on Agent dispatches — LOCKED

Reading an Agent's `.output` file overflows the orchestrator's context with the full JSONL transcript. The role file must explicitly say "do NOT call TaskOutput on a local_agent task_id." For Bash background tasks, `Read` on the output file is the right tool; `TaskOutput` itself is still deprecated per Anthropic.

### B2. `Monitor` is the canonical orchestrator push channel — LOCKED

Not a poll-cron, not an ad-hoc bw poll inside the conversation. The orchestrator fires `Monitor` with `persistent: true` at dispatch time; the orchestrator's chat receives push events; the orchestrator TaskStops the Monitor when the dispatch completes.

### B3. `task_id` materialization to bw is mandatory at dispatch time — LOCKED

Without it, the orchestrator cannot recover the task_id later in the session (no enumeration tool exists, per issues #29011 / #49140). The first `bw comment` after every background dispatch carries the task_id.

### B4. Canonical poll-loop template lives in role files — LOCKED

`MAJOR_PLINY.md` and `MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` carry the canonical bash poll-loop template (Step 3 above). DAEDALUS does NOT need to invent the template per-dispatch; the orchestrator copies the template at dispatch time with the dispatch ticket ID substituted.

### B5. CAPTAIN-side `Monitor` and `run_in_background` Bash forbidden — LOCKED via Ticket A

This ticket re-states Ticket A's A5 for completeness; both tickets should ship together so the discipline is consistent across orchestrator and CAPTAIN role files.

### B6. PushNotification is orthogonal, not part of the orchestrator-CAPTAIN bridge — LOCKED

Reserved for PRINCIPAL-actionable events (escalations, blockers, ship/no-ship). The orchestrator-CAPTAIN bridge does not use PushNotification.

## Substrate touch-points

1. **`substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md`** — new section on background-dispatch hygiene. Covers: load deferred tools at session start (Step 1); dispatch sequence (Step 2); canonical poll-loop template (Step 3); completion cleanup (Step 4); PushNotification orthogonality (Step 5). LOCKED decisions B1-B6 recorded as the canonical patterns.

2. **`substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md`** — analogous section for pair-programming-mode CAPTAIN dispatches by POLYBIUS. Same patterns, POLYBIUS-specific framing.

3. **`substrate/operating-disciplines.md`** — cross-ref to MAJOR_PLINY / MAJOR_POLYBIUS sections; brief mention in the comms-hygiene section that bridges with Ticket A's universal CAPTAIN discipline.

4. **Agent-author template / skill** — new CAPTAIN dispatchers inherit the canonical pattern by default; the dispatch sequence is in the scaffold, not re-invented per orchestrator.

## Gauntlet shape

Full gauntlet — DAEDALUS + ARGUS + ADA + VERA + CATO + ZENO. Substrate-prose edits across 3-4 files plus the canonical poll-loop template (which needs to be empirically tested — VERA dispatches its own probe of the template via a smoke beat).

VERA's probe: run the canonical poll-loop template against a real bw ticket; confirm new comments emit one line each; confirm `last=` cursor advances correctly; confirm transient `bw show` failures (network, lock contention) don't kill the monitor (note the `|| true` clause).

## Cross-references

- **Ticket A (universal CAPTAIN heartbeat discipline):** complementary; ships in the same arc.
- **Ticket C (confabulation discipline):** same empirical anchor; verb-level not architectural.
- **stoa--ay1:** adaptive polling cadence — partially superseded by Monitor pattern (Monitor is push, not poll, so cadence is event-driven rather than time-driven).
- **stoa--ivc:** radio-check pattern — this ticket sharpens the transport (Monitor + bw) for the radio-check.

## Sequencing

P2. Substrate-DNA discipline. Same arc as Ticket A + Ticket C. After Arc 23 (`stoa--pmp`) closes. NOT folded into Arc 22 (`stoa--jru`).

## Out of scope

- Adding `TaskOutput` on Agent paths (it's deprecated and unsafe for Agents)
- Building a custom enumeration tool for in-flight background tasks (Anthropic's surface; out of substrate)
- Auto-cleanup of orphaned Bash from CAPTAINs (issue #23154; OS-level workaround needed, not substrate)
- Replacing Monitor with a custom poll loop in the orchestrator's own Bash (would re-introduce poll churn — Monitor's push semantics are the point)

## Authorship attribution

Authored by Denson Smith via POLYBIUS conversation, 2026-05-12. All edits to substrate land under Denson Smith authorship.

comments.text:
Cross-tier finding 2026-05-12 — SendMessage docs-vs-registry drift confirmed universal in Claude Code Desktop harness.

Two empirical probes (ariadne PLINY worktree session + POLYBIUS the-stoa Desktop session) both ran 'ToolSearch select:SendMessage' and got 'No matching deferred tools found'. SendMessage is also absent from the deferred-tools enumeration. Yet the Agent tool's own description tells dispatchers 'use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the to field to resume it with full context', and every Agent dispatch's return value embeds the same instruction.

ariadne PLINY designed a seeder gate-with-resume brief depending on SendMessage. Brief contract couldn't be fulfilled at run-time. ariadne PLINY pivoted to PLINY-direct-execute (mechanical fallback worked). Full diagnostic at C:/Users/denso/claude_projects/ariadne-core-workspace/.claude/worktrees/lucid-lalande-b1801f/HUMAN_relay_user_polybius_sendmessage_gap_2026-05-12.md.

Substrate implication for stoa--nvl's DAEDALUS design: add a 'harness-capability check at brief-authoring time' discipline. Rule shape: 'Before writing a dispatch brief clause that depends on tool X, run ToolSearch (or equivalent) and verify X is in the registry. If not, design around its absence (use bw-substrate coordination instead).' This is verify-then-execute applied to tooling, not state. Pairs with stoa--nvl B1 (load deferred tools at session start) — but extends it: don't just LOAD documented tools, also VERIFY they exist before depending on them in a brief.

Plus: the Monitor + bw-poll bridge architecture stoa--nvl already names IS the workable absence-aware pattern. PLINY's mistake was naming SendMessage in the brief instead of relying on the bw-bridge architecture POLYBIUS had already prescribed.

Arc 24 DAEDALUS folds this finding into the brief-design section. New discipline-bullet for nvl's substrate prose: 'Brief authoring is a verify-then-execute exercise. Any tool the brief depends on must be empirically present in the registry at brief-authoring time. Documentation alone is insufficient evidence.'

Correction to my previous comment 2026-05-12 — confabulation discipline applied to my own commentary.

I characterized the SendMessage finding as 'docs-vs-implementation drift.' That was wrong. Web verification (searched Anthropic Claude Code GitHub issues + Claude Code Changelog X post about v2.1.77) shows:

- SendMessage IS a real, documented Anthropic tool, formally added to Claude Code 2.1.77.
- It is gated behind the agent-teams feature flag (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 or current equivalent).
- PRINCIPAL's machine does not have the flag enabled, so SendMessage is absent from the registry.
- The actual bug is that the Agent tool's description does NOT condition the SendMessage advice on the flag state — it tells everyone to use SendMessage regardless.
- Bug is already filed upstream as anthropics/claude-code#42737 ('SendMessage tool unavailable without agent teams feature, breaking agent resume') and anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python#716. No new upstream filing needed.
- Even when the flag is enabled, anthropics/claude-code#48160 reports subagents cannot originate SendMessage — only the orchestrator can.

Substrate implication for DAEDALUS's nvl design: the brief-design discipline ('verify tool availability before depending on it in a brief') still applies — the discipline is cause-agnostic. But the substrate prose should NOT describe SendMessage as a 'drift' or 'missing' — it's feature-gated. Use precise wording: 'gated behind agent-teams experimental feature; absent without the flag.'

Also: the Monitor + bw-poll bridge architecture nvl already names is the right pattern WHETHER OR NOT the agent-teams flag is enabled, because even with the flag, subagents-originating-SendMessage doesn't work (#48160). The bw-bridge is the canonical CAPTAIN-side mechanism either way.

DAEDALUS reads this correction along with the prior comment when authoring nvl's substrate prose.

SUPERSEDING CORRECTIVE 2026-05-12 — replaces my two prior comments on this ticket.

PRINCIPAL caught polluting agent-teams architecture into nvl's scope. Both prior comments did this: the first by framing SendMessage absence as "docs-vs-implementation drift" (cause-agnostic but framing pollution), the second by importing Anthropic's agent-teams feature scope (experimental flag, agent-teams paradigm, #48160) into a substrate ticket about subagent dispatch hygiene. Both wrong. Substrate prose for nvl must describe what WE use, not what Anthropic's other feature scopes offer.

DAEDALUS — when authoring nvl's substrate prose, use these as input:

1. **`_drafts/coordination-primer-monitor-and-bw.md`** — canonical primer authored cold (no prior knowledge assumed). Four parts: Monitor mechanism + parameters + pitfalls + Stoa-tier rules; bw command surface + our conventions; the orchestrator-CAPTAIN bridge architecture; explicit "what we are NOT using" (agent-teams, SendMessage, TaskOutput on Agents, polling agent introspection). ~12-15 pages. Intended landing: `substrate/coordination-primer.md` (new file; install.sh deploy-list must add it per stoa--14u smoke-beat discipline).

2. **`_drafts/role-file-coordination-sections.md`** — per-role digest drafts (~30-60 lines each) that go INTO each role file rather than bloating them. Grouped:
   - MAJOR_POLYBIUS section: top-tier dispatch + cross-tier coordination + escalation triggers
   - MAJOR_PLINY section: canonical CAPTAIN-dispatch sequence (Agent → task_id-to-bw → Monitor → heartbeat-react → TaskStop)
   - Pair-programmer MAJOR section: cross-reference PLINY
   - 10 CAPTAIN sections: same four-rule cooperative-yield discipline + seat-specific heartbeat shape + forbidden tools (Monitor / background Bash / Agent dispatch)
   - operating-disciplines.md universal section: architecture summary + two-tier model + four CAPTAIN rules + orchestrator dispatch sequence + what-we-don't-use

3. **The three ticket bodies** (stoa--odh, stoa--nvl, stoa--ioy) carry the discipline statements + Phase-A LOCKED decisions + empirical anchors. Treat as additional spec input.

Substrate prose for nvl should reflect:
- Our toolkit is: Monitor (orchestrator-side push), TaskStop (orchestrator-side abort), Agent (orchestrator-side dispatch), Bash + bw CLI (universal substrate coordination).
- We work around basic-subagent-dispatch limitations using bw as the cross-session substrate.
- We are NOT in Anthropic's agent-teams paradigm. Do not reference agent-teams concepts in nvl prose.
- The Monitor + bw bridge IS the absence-aware pattern that works regardless of which Anthropic feature scopes are or aren't available.

Brief-design discipline (cause-agnostic) still applies: verify tool availability via ToolSearch at session start; do not write briefs depending on tools not in the registry. Substrate prose should describe this as a positive discipline ("verify tools you use") rather than via reference to a missing-tool example.

Two prior polluted comments stand in history but are superseded by this comment. DAEDALUS treats them as cautionary examples of confabulation discipline failure (cited an X tracker as Anthropic; mixed agent-teams architecture into subagent-dispatch scope), not as substrate spec.
